verdict.rationale: Reflect's import/export docs state that notes can always be exported to an open format such as HTML or Markdown, which covers the core of archive portability. The evidence does not document a JSON export, the structure or fidelity of the exported files (for example, whether backlinks and metadata survive), or any independent confirmation that export works. The reflect.app 'local Markdown files' claims sit awkwardly beside the same page's end-to-end encryption claims, so they add little weight. missing for 10: documented JSON export, documented export format spec/fidelity (links, metadata, attachments), hands-on or independent corroboration of a full-archive export

support.subject: As a researcher, my notes are stored or exportable in open, documented formats (Markdown, JSON) so my archive outlives the vendor

citations.quote: you can always export it into an open format (like HTML or Markdown).
An open-source note-taking app with daily notes, backlinks, and local Markdown files.
